name: Bull flag
shape: A sharp advance, then an orderly pause in it.
description: The advance is what this screen selects for: a run of at least 10% in three to five sessions, carried on above-average volume, in a stock still holding its 20-day line. The pause afterwards only has to be orderly. It is listed because every other screen here needs a base, and a stock that has just run hard does not have one — so a strong name resting after a move is invisible to the rest of the site. The level shown is the top of the pause. This shape has never been tested on this site. The out-of-sample study behind the base screens found no measurable edge in their structural parts — only in relative strength — and no equivalent study has been run against trendline shapes at all. Read this screen as a description of what the chart is doing, which is checkable, and not as a reason to expect anything.

concepts.title: The pause
concepts.text: A short, orderly drift after it.

funnel.title: The liquid US universe
funnel.text: US common stocks over $5, market cap over $300M, and at least $5M traded a day over the last 20 sessions.

funnel.title: There is a pole
funnel.text: A move of at least 10% runs into the pause.

funnel.title: Sharp, not gradual
funnel.text: The advance took no more than 5 sessions.

funnel.title: The pause is orderly
funnel.text: High to low across the pause is no more than 8%.

funnel.title: The pole carried volume
funnel.text: Volume through the advance ran at 1x its normal.

funnel.title: The pause is shallow
funnel.text: No more than 0.5 of the pole has been given back.

funnel.title: Short enough to be a flag
funnel.text: The pause is no longer than 7 sessions.

funnel.title: Leadership
funnel.text: Relative strength rating of 70 or better.

funnel_preface: Every number below is a dial you can move in Filters.

params.label: Smallest move that counts as a pole
params.funnel_text: A move of at least {value}% runs into the pause.
params.help: A flag is a pause inside a move. Without a move in front of it, it is just a quiet fortnight, and this is the line between the two.

params.label: Longest run that counts as a pole
params.funnel_text: The advance took no more than {value} sessions.
params.help: A flag interrupts a sharp move. A gentle climb over six weeks is a trend, and the screens for those are elsewhere.

params.label: How far the pause may wander, high to low
params.funnel_text: High to low across the pause is no more than {value}%.
params.help: The pause has to be calmer than the run that caused it, and the run is at least ten per cent — so a pause allowed to swing wider than that is not a pause, it is the move breaking down. Eight leaves margin under the smallest pole that qualifies. Loosening further does keep finding names (sixteen at eight per cent, twenty-one at twelve), but they are the ones where the pause is as violent as the advance, which is the thing this screen is supposed to exclude. Three per cent was the opposite mistake: it asked the pause to be calmer than any real stock manages and left two names on the whole market.

params.label: Volume through the pole
params.funnel_text: Volume through the advance ran at {value}x its normal.
params.help: A move nobody traded is a gap or a thin print. The volume is what makes the advance evidence of anything.

params.label: How much of the pole it may give back
params.funnel_text: No more than {value} of the pole has been given back.
params.help: A drift that surrenders most of the move it is pausing inside is not a pause; it is the move ending.

params.label: Longest pause we'll still call a flag
params.funnel_title: Short enough to be a flag
params.funnel_text: The pause is no longer than {value} sessions.
params.help: Flags are brief by definition. A long enough pause is a base, and this site has six screens for those.

params.label: Shortest pause we'll accept
params.help: Fewer bars than this is a gap in the move rather than a pause in it.

params.label: Lowest RS rating we'll accept
params.funnel_text: Relative strength rating of {value} or better.
params.help: Where the stock's 3, 6 and 12-month return ranks against every other name in the universe, 1 to 99. This is the one filter with published statistical support behind it.

params.label: How recent counts as fresh
params.help: A breakout stays in the fresh bucket for this many sessions before it moves to climbing.

trade_steps.title: Buy the breakout
trade_steps.text: As it pushes through the pivot.

trade_steps.title: Set a safety net
trade_steps.text: An automatic exit if it drops about 8% from where you got in.

trade_steps.title: Lock in "no loss"
trade_steps.text: Once it is up enough, move that net to where you started.

trade_steps.title: Ride the trend
trade_steps.text: Raise the net as it climbs.

trade_steps_preface: Risk is decided before entry — about 1.5% of capital on any one trade.
